title: Online DPO (v0.71.31)
description: Online DPO (v0.71.31) — soup train with task: online_dpo puts an LLM judge in the training loop: it samples two on-policy completions per prompt, a swap-debiased pairwise judge (or a reward model) names the winner (chosen) and the loser (rejected), and the model takes a DPO step on that fresh pair. Wraps TRL OnlineDPOTrainer; config online_dpo_judge or reward_model (exactly one), online_dpo_loss_type sigmoid|ipo, online_dpo_max_new_tokens; transformers + text only. Proof-of-mechanism on SmolLM2-135M with a synthetic judge (not a production RLHF claim); on the supported trl range (0.29 up to, but not including, 1.0) it uses TRL's pairwise-judge path with Soup's swap-debiased judge, and since v0.75.2 online_dpo_judge is checked when the config loads and refuses a private IP address.

blocks.html:
Online DPO (v0.71.31)

soup train with task: online_dpo puts an LLM judge (or a reward model) in the training loop. Each step samples two on-policy completions per prompt, a pairwise judge names the winner chosen and the loser rejected, and the model takes a DPO step on that fresh, self-generated pair. It wraps TRL's OnlineDPOTrainer, and it is transformers + text only (prompt-only data, like GRPO).

This is the training face of the v0.71.31 judge-in-the-loop suite: the same swap-debiased judge also mines data with best-of-N, grows it with Evol-Instruct, and decides SHIP with a pairwise win-rate in soup ship.

Config

blocks.code:
base: HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M-Instruct
task: online_dpo
data:
  train: ./data/prompts.jsonl      # prompt-only rows; see the note on row shape below
training:
  online_dpo_judge: "ollama://llama3.1"   # a pairwise judge (ollama:// | https:// | http://localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1])
  # OR set a reward model instead of a judge (exactly one of the two):
  # reward_model: ./my-reward-model
  online_dpo_loss_type: sigmoid           # sigmoid | ipo
  online_dpo_max_new_tokens: 64
  dpo_beta: 0.1
  gradient_checkpointing: true   # since v0.77.0 the default false turns it off here
  lora: { r: 8, alpha: 16, target_modules: auto }

soup train --config online_dpo.yaml
# or start from the ready-made recipe:
soup recipes use online-dpo-smollm2-135m

blocks.html:
Row shape. The data goes through the normal format detection first, so a row has to be one the loader recognises. A chat row with no assistant turn, {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hi"}]}, passes soup train --dry-run as chatml; a bare {"prompt": "Say hi"} row does not (Cannot detect format. Keys found: {'prompt'}, exit 1) unless you wrap it in a recognised shape. A dpo-format file is recognised, and online DPO uses only its prompts; since v0.76.1 the dpo converter hands such a row's prompt over as a message list (the leading turns the two answers share, or the string as one user turn when they share none; a string beside answers that share turns is not read), and online DPO reads a message-list prompt the same way as messages (#1866). Upstream's own check of v0.76.1 did not run online_dpo.

Config fields

FieldDefaultMeaning
online_dpo_judge(none)Judge URL (ollama://model, https://..., or http://localhost / http://127.0.0.1 / http://[::1]; the loopback spellings are one shared set since v0.76.0). Mutually exclusive with reward_model. Since v0.75.2 a URL naming a private, link-local or reserved IP address is refused when the config loads, not when the trainer starts, so soup train --dry-run catches it; use a hostname (private addresses refused). A numeric-only host that is not a valid IPv4 address (10.0.0.256, 4294967296) is refused at load as well (online_dpo_judge: an all-numeric host that is not a valid IPv4 address is not allowed (SSRF protection); use a valid IPv4 address or a hostname).
reward_model(none)A reward model to score completions instead of a judge. Exactly one of judge / reward_model must be set.
online_dpo_loss_typesigmoidsigmoid (DPO) or ipo.
online_dpo_max_new_tokens64Tokens to sample per completion (1..4096).
betavia dpo_betaThe DPO temperature; reuses the existing dpo_beta.

Two behaviours that follow from the generation loop (v0.76.0, #1223): task: online_dpo neither evaluates nor holds out data.val_split, because evaluating means generating. The split is ignored, every row trains, and the run prints Note: data.val_split is ignored for task=online_dpo because evaluation means generation, so every row trains. training.eval_steps is refused at config load (training.eval_steps is not supported for task='online_dpo' because online DPO's evaluate() crashes on prompt-only rows; ...). --fsdp and --deepspeed now reach this trainer (#1204); through v0.75.2 the wrapper stored them and never passed them to its trainer arguments.

Gradient checkpointing (v0.77.0, #797, #1778). training.gradient_checkpointing now reaches this trainer. With the default false, online DPO trains with checkpointing off, where TRL's own default (on) used to apply whatever the config said, so a config that never set the key uses more activation memory than it did. Set training.gradient_checkpointing: true, as the fence above does, to keep the memory you had; upstream's shipped online-DPO recipe and examples now set it (#1923).

The cross-validator requires backend: transformers and modality: text, and rejects both-set or neither-set judge / reward_model, plus any online_dpo_* field left non-default when the task is not online_dpo.

How the judge is used (and a per-version note)

The judge is Soup's JudgeEvaluator adapted to TRL, swap-debiased: it compares the two completions in both orders and only records a winner when (A,B) and (B,A) agree, so position bias cannot leak a preference.

The judge is chosen by capability, not by version: Soup asks the installed trl OnlineDPOTrainer whether it accepts a pairwise judge=.

  • On the supported range (trl>=0.29.0,<1.0.0, which is what [train] installs) the swap-debiased pairwise judge is used (judge=).
  • On a trl that has dropped judge= (trl 1.x removed pairwise judges, and is outside the declared range) the same JudgeEvaluator is adapted to a pointwise reward_funcs= scorer.

Same judge model either way; the comparison shape differs with what the installed trl accepts. The upper bound sits below trl 1 because that migration is separate work, so the pointwise branch is there for a mismatched install, not the normal path.

When the judge cannot rank a pair (v0.76.0)

The judge answers "no winner" for a tie, a failed or unreadable call, or a verdict that changes when the two completions are swapped. On the online_dpo_judge path such a pair now adds exactly zero gradient, and the loss is the mean over the pairs the judge did rank in each batch (each micro-batch, under gradient accumulation) (#1225). The run logs judge/invalid_rate, the share it could not rank, with a WARNING the first time and on every step that ranked nothing, and the logged loss and train_loss average only the batches that ranked a pair. A step that ranked nothing still takes an optimizer step, so AdamW momentum and weight decay keep moving the weights. Once 32 pairs in a row go unranked, training stops with an error naming the judge. A run that ranked no pair at all fails the same way at the end instead of saving an adapter. The end-of-run line reads the judge could not rank N of M pairs (x%); they were left out of the loss. The reward_model path is unchanged.

An unreachable judge is reported as unavailable (it is not scored as a tie) by the other judge-backed commands since v0.76.0 (#1447); in Online DPO a failed call leaves its pair unranked, as above.

Since v0.77.0 a judge reply is bounded to 1 MiB of decoded bytes (#1819, #1929): a larger one is refused before it is parsed, its body is not logged, and the call is reported as an unavailable judge, so in Online DPO that pair is left unranked too.

(Since closed in v0.76.0: through v0.75.2, trl 0.29's OnlineDPOTrainer built mask = rank == 0, so every unranked pair trained as a win for the second completion and the loss was averaged over all pairs. With the judge server down, a whole run learned arbitrary labels and finished normally.)

Re-run this

If you trainedWhat was wrongWhat to do
task: online_dpo with training.online_dpo_judgeA pair the judge could not rank (a tie, a failed or unreadable call, or an order-dependent verdict) trained as a win for the second completion, with nothing saying so (#1225)Re-run, especially if the judge was remote or flaky

Honesty

Proof-of-mechanism only. Online DPO was validated on SmolLM2-135M with a synthetic length-preferring judge on CPU (rewards/* and objective/kl logged), not a production RLHF claim. The 4-bit path is code-correct but hardware-gated (validated at quantization: none on CPU; real QLoRA online-DPO needs a bigger GPU). Scale validation is an open community ask (issue #286).
